docs.text: HardFOC tools ESP-IDF Project Tools ¶ Shell and Python scripts that build, flash and monitor every app of a multi-app ESP-IDF project. The apps, ESP-IDF versions, build types and target are written once, in app_config.yml, and the same scripts run on your machine and in CI. Quickstart build_app.sh Source on GitHub The scripts live inside your project, usually as a submodule at examples/esp32/scripts , next to the app_config.yml they read. Every HardFOC driver, hf-core and the board HALs use them for their ESP32 examples, and hf-espidf-ci-tools runs them in GitHub Actions. One configuration file, every script Figure description and sources From top to bottom. app_config.yml in the ESP-IDF project lists the apps, ESP-IDF versions, build types and target. Two readers parse it: config_loader.sh, which the shell scripts source, and the Python scripts generate_matrix.py and get_app_info.py. The commands that source config_loader.sh (read from the scripts) sit on top of them. build_app.sh drives idf.py and writes one build folder per app, build type, target and ESP-IDF version under builds/. In CI, hf-espidf-ci-tools runs generate_matrix.py and build_app.sh. docs.text: app_config.yml ¶ Every key of the project's app_config.yml , its default and which script reads it. The file sits in the project directory ( Project layout ). The shell scripts read it through config_loader.sh ; generate_matrix.py and get_app_info.py read it with PyYAML. Example ¶ --- version : "1.0" metadata : project : "ESP32 TMC9660 Driver Examples" default_app : "bldc_comprehensive_test" default_build_type : "Release" target : "esp32c6" idf_versions : [ "release/v5.5" , "release/v5.4" ] build_types : [[ "Debug" , "Release" ], [ "Debug" ]] apps : bldc_comprehensive_test : description : "BLDC motor test with Hall sensors and velocity control" source_file : "bldc_comprehensive_test.cpp" idf_versions : [ "release/v5.5" ] build_types : [ "Debug" , "Release" ] ci_enabled : true featured : true build_config : build_directory_pattern : "build-app-{app_type}-type-{build_type}-target-{target}-idf-{idf_version}" project_name_pattern : "esp32_{app_type}_app" ci_config : exclude_combinations : - { app_name : bldc_comprehensive_test , build_type : Release } metadata ¶ Key Default Read by Meaning default_app none build_app.sh , flash_app.sh App used when no app is given default_build_type none build_app.sh , flash_app.sh Build type used when none is given target esp32c6 ( generate_matrix.py ) all Chip passed to ESP-IDF ( IDF_TARGET ) idf_versions ["release/v5.5"] all ESP-IDF branches or tags; the first is the default and is installed first build_types [["Debug", "Release"]] all One list per entry of idf_versions , by position project none none (descriptive) Project title apps.<name> ¶ The key is the app name used on the command line ( gpio_test ) and passed to CMake as APP_TYPE . Key Default Meaning source_file required (or source_files ) File passed to CMake as APP_SOURCE_FILE source_files none A list; the first entry is passed as APP_SOURCE_FILE description none Shown by build_app.sh list ; generate_matrix.py --validate warns when missing idf_versions metadata.idf_versions ESP-IDF versions for this app build_types from metadata A flat list for every version, or one list per version ci_enabled true false leaves the app out of the CI matrix featured false Listed first by build_app.sh list and flash_app.sh list (with yq ) target metadata.target Read only by idf_flash_monitor.sh ; build_app.sh and the matrix use metadata.target category , tags , dependencies none Descriptive; no script reads them build_config ¶ Key Meaning build_directory_pattern Build folder name under builds/ , with {app_type} , {build_type} , {target} , {idf_version} project_name_pattern ESP-IDF project name, with {app_type} ; used to find the .bin to flash build_types.<name> Descriptive (flags, defines); CMake sets the real flags A pattern that is missing or empty falls back to its default, with or without yq : build-app-{app_type}-type-{build_type}-target-{target}-idf-{idf_version} and esp32_iid_{app_type}_app . Without yq the scripts always use these defaults and ignore the keys. ci_config ¶ Key Meaning exclude_combinations Matrix entries to drop: an entry is dropped when every key of an item matches ( app_name , build_type , idf_version , target ) Other keys under ci_config ( timeout_minutes , fail_fast , special_apps ) are not read; the CI workflow sets its own timeout and fail-fast: false . How the matrix and the local scripts agree ¶ build_app.sh refuses a combination the configuration does not allow ( is_valid_combination in config_loader.sh ), and generate_matrix.py emits exactly the allowed combinations. When an ESP-IDF version is not given, build_app.sh picks the first version of the app whose build types include the requested one. Keep arrays on one line without yq The fallback parser reads idf_versions and build_types from a single line, and reads app names between apps: and build_config: . Write arrays in the inline form shown above and keep build_config after apps .

docs.text: build_app.sh ¶ Build one app of the project for one build type and ESP-IDF version, in its own build folder. ./scripts/build_app.sh [ options ] <app> <build_type> [ idf_version ] ./scripts/build_app.sh list | combinations | info <app> | validate <app> <build_type> [ idf_version ] Arguments ¶ Argument Meaning app An app name from app_config.yml ; default metadata.default_app build_type Debug , Release or another type the app allows; default metadata.default_build_type idf_version ESP-IDF branch or tag, for example release/v5.5 ; default: the first of the app's versions that allows the build type Option Environment Effect --clean / --no-clean CLEAN=1 / CLEAN=0 Delete the build folder first, or keep it (incremental, the default) --use-cache / --no-cache USE_CCACHE=1 / USE_CCACHE=0 ccache on or off (passed as IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE ) --project-path <path> PROJECT_PATH The project directory ( Project layout ) --secret <hex> ESPNOW_PAIRING_SECRET ESP-NOW pairing secret ( Project layout ) -h , --help Usage Options can go anywhere on the line. Commands ¶ Command Prints list Featured apps, all apps with descriptions, build types, ESP-IDF versions combinations Every allowed app, build type and ESP-IDF version info <app> The allowed combinations of one app validate <app> <build_type> [idf_version] Whether the combination is allowed What a build does ¶ Checks the app, the build type and the full combination against app_config.yml ; a combination the file does not allow stops here, with the allowed ones listed. If idf.py is not on the PATH , installs (when missing) and exports the ESP-IDF version from ~/esp ( manage_idf.sh ). Sets IDF_TARGET from metadata.target . Reads the app's source file with get_app_info.py source_file <app> . Runs idf.py -B <build folder> reconfigure with the CMake variables , then idf.py build . Writes size.txt ( idf.py size ), size.json when supported, size.info and size.meta into the build folder. Output ¶ File in the build folder Content <project_name>.bin , .elf , .map Firmware, from build_config.project_name_pattern size.txt idf.py size output size.json idf.py size-json output, when the ESP-IDF version has it size.info APP= , BUILD= , IDF= , TARGET= , PROJECT_NAME= , BUILD_DIR= lines; read by the CI size report size.meta ELF_FILE= and MAP_FILE= paths Examples ¶ ./scripts/build_app.sh gpio_test Release # default ESP-IDF version for Release ./scripts/build_app.sh gpio_test Debug release/v5.4 --clean # a specific version, from scratch ./scripts/build_app.sh --project-path ../fw gpio_test Debug # scripts outside the project CLEAN = 1 USE_CCACHE = 0 ./scripts/build_app.sh gpio_test Debug # the same through the environment Next: flash_app.sh .

docs.text: Using in CI ¶ How GitHub Actions builds every app with these scripts, through the reusable workflow in hf-espidf-ci-tools. hf-espidf-ci-tools ru-build.yml runs, for a caller that pins @v1 : generate_matrix.py (no arguments) for the matrix; for each entry, inside the espressif/idf:<idf_version_docker> image, build_app.sh --project-path <project_dir> <app> <build_type> <idf_version> ; an upload of <project_dir>/build* (the builds/ folder) as fw-<app>-<idf>-<build type> ; on pull requests, a size table from each build's size.info and size.txt . The workflow requires generate_matrix.py , build_app.sh and config_loader.sh in the tools folder, and installs requirements.txt when it is there. The caller ¶ jobs : build : uses : hardfoc/hf-espidf-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : write with : project_dir : examples/esp32 project_tools_dir : examples/esp32/scripts Inputs, permissions and failure modes are on the ru-build page . Keep the matrix and the build on the same file ¶ The workflow runs generate_matrix.py without --project-path , so the matrix comes from examples/esp32/app_config.yml (from the repository root) or from app_config.yml above the scripts. Keep the project in examples/esp32 with the scripts in examples/esp32/scripts , the HardFOC layout, and both read the same file. Check locally what CI will build ¶ python3 examples/esp32/scripts/generate_matrix.py --project-path examples/esp32 --format yaml ./examples/esp32/scripts/build_app.sh combinations

docs.text: flash_app.sh ¶ Flash an app to a board and open the serial monitor, building it first when no build exists. ./scripts/flash_app.sh [ operation ] [ app ] [ build_type ] [ idf_version ] [ options ] ./scripts/flash_app.sh [ app ] [ build_type ] [ idf_version ] [ operation ] [ options ] Operations ¶ Operation Does flash_monitor (default) idf.py flash monitor with the app's build folder flash Flash only monitor Monitor only; uses the newest build folder for symbol decoding when there is one size idf.py size , size-components and a JSON memory summary of an existing build list The apps, build types and ESP-IDF versions ports The serial ports that look like ESP32 boards The operation can be the first or the last word. Missing app, build type and version come from metadata.default_app , metadata.default_build_type and the first entry of metadata.idf_versions . Options ¶ Option Environment Effect --port <dev> , -p <dev> ESPPORT Serial port; the flag wins over the variable --log [name] Copy the monitor output to <project>/logs/<name>_<timestamp>.log (default name <app>_<build_type> or monitor ) --project-path <path> PROJECT_PATH The project directory -h , --help Usage Finding the port ¶ Without --port or ESPPORT the script looks for /dev/ttyACM* and /dev/ttyUSB* on Linux, and /dev/cu.usbmodem* , /dev/cu.usbserial* , /dev/cu.SLAB_USBtoUART* , /dev/cu.CP210* , /dev/cu.CH340* (then the /dev/tty.* equivalents) on macOS. One port is used directly; with several it asks which one, and takes the first after 30 seconds. ./scripts/flash_app.sh ports and detect_ports.sh show what it finds. Building first ¶ Before flashing, the script checks for <build folder>/<project_name>.bin . When it is missing it deletes the incomplete folder and runs build_app.sh <app> <build_type> ; that build uses the default ESP-IDF version for the build type, not an idf_version given to flash_app.sh . docs.text: generate_matrix.py ¶ Turn app_config.yml into the build matrix of a GitHub Actions job: one entry per app, ESP-IDF version and build type. python3 scripts/generate_matrix.py # JSON on stdout python3 scripts/generate_matrix.py --validate --verbose # check the file first python3 scripts/generate_matrix.py --filter gpio_test --format yaml Options ¶ Argument Values Default Description --help / -h flag - Show help message --output / -o value - Output file path --format / -f json , yaml json Output format --filter value - Filter output for specific app --verbose / -v flag - Verbose output --validate flag - Validate configuration --project-path / -p value - Path to project directory containing app_config.yml Without --project-path the script looks for examples/esp32/app_config.yml , app_config.yml , ../app_config.yml , ../../examples/esp32/app_config.yml (all from the current directory) and finally app_config.yml in the folder above the script, and uses the first that exists. Output ¶ { "include" : [ { "idf_version" : "release/v5.5" , "idf_version_docker" : "release-v5.5" , "idf_version_file" : "release_v5_5" , "build_type" : "Debug" , "app_name" : "gpio_test" , "target" : "esp32c6" , "config_source" : "global" } ]} Field Meaning idf_version As written in app_config.yml ; passed to build_app.sh idf_version_docker / replaced by - : the espressif/idf image tag and the artifact name idf_version_file / and . replaced by _ : the build folder suffix build_type , app_name , target The combination config_source app when the app overrides idf_versions or build_types , else global Rules ¶ Apps with ci_enabled: false are skipped. Each app uses its own idf_versions , or metadata.idf_versions . Build types: the app's flat build_types list for every version; or its nested list by position; or metadata.build_types by position; Debug and Release when a position has no list. metadata.target , default esp32c6 . Entries matching an item of ci_config.exclude_combinations on every key are dropped. --validate fails on a missing metadata or apps section, an empty apps , or build_types / idf_versions that are not lists of strings, and warns on missing defaults, descriptions or source files. --validate and --verbose print their messages on standard output before the matrix, so leave them out where the output is parsed as JSON (use --output to write the matrix to a file instead).

docs.text: manage_idf.sh ¶ Install, list, export and switch the ESP-IDF versions that app_config.yml asks for. ./scripts/manage_idf.sh <command> [ version ] [ --force ] [ --project-path <path> ] Commands ¶ Command Does install [--force] Clones every version in metadata.idf_versions into ~/esp/esp-idf-<version> (with submodules), runs install.sh esp32c6 , and points ~/esp/esp-idf at the first. --force deletes and re-clones existing ones list The versions installed under ~/esp export <version> Sources that version's export.sh in the script's own shell switch <version> Points the ~/esp/esp-idf symlink at the version update <version> git pull the version and its submodules, then install.sh esp32c6 clean <version> Deletes the version's folder status The current ESP-IDF environment The folder name replaces every character other than letters, digits, . , _ and - with - : release/v5.5 is installed in ~/esp/esp-idf-release-v5.5 . Tools go to ~/.espressif/ as usual. switch , update , clean and export also find a version installed under the older name with / replaced by _ ( ~/esp/esp-idf-release_v5.5 ), so machines set up by earlier versions of these scripts keep working. list and status show both names as release/v5.5 . Using an installed version ¶ build_app.sh exports the right version itself when idf.py is not on the PATH . In an interactive shell, source the version directly: . ~/esp/esp-idf-release-v5.5/export.sh export runs in a child process, so it cannot change the calling shell. Tools are installed for esp32c6 install and update run install.sh esp32c6 whatever metadata.target says. For another chip, run install.sh <target> in the version's folder once.

docs.text: Ports and logs ¶ Find the board's serial port, watch it come and go, and read the monitor logs flash_app.sh --log writes. detect_ports.sh ¶ ./scripts/detect_ports.sh # ports that look like ESP32 boards ./scripts/detect_ports.sh --verbose # with USB details and permissions ./scripts/detect_ports.sh --test-connection # also open each port It lists candidate ports on Linux and macOS, checks that you can open them and prints the usual fixes (the dialout group, a cable without data lines, a missing USB-to-UART driver, a port held by another program). watch_serial_port.sh ¶ Polls /dev/ttyACM* and /dev/ttyUSB* every INTERVAL_SEC seconds (default 2) and prints and logs CONNECTED / DISCONNECTED when the set changes, with an export ESPPORT=... hint. The log goes to LOG (default /tmp/hf-vortex-esp-port-watch.log ). Linux device names only. INTERVAL_SEC = 1 ./scripts/watch_serial_port.sh idf_flash_monitor.sh ¶ The plain ESP-IDF flow for an existing build, without flash_app.sh 's port search and auto-build: export ESPPORT = /dev/ttyACM0 ./scripts/idf_flash_monitor.sh gpio_test Release # idf.py -C <project> -B <build> -p $ESPPORT flash monitor ./scripts/idf_flash_monitor.sh gpio_test Release --no-reset # extra arguments go to idf.py It needs ESPPORT , an ESP-IDF environment and the build folder ( build_app.sh first). Without arguments it uses the app vortex_led_ws2812_smoke and Release . It honours a per-app target in app_config.yml . manage_logs.sh ¶ Reads the logs in <project>/logs/ : Command Does list [pattern] Every log (names in reverse order) with date, time and size; only names containing pattern when given view <log> Shows one log (in less on a terminal) search <pattern> Searches every log; prints the first 5 matching lines of each clean [days] Deletes logs older than days (default 30) after asking stats Count, total size, oldest and newest, and logs per app latest The last 20 lines of the newest log tail <log> [lines] The last lines lines of one log (default 50); add --follow to keep printing new lines grep <log> <pattern> Matching lines of one log with line numbers; exit status 1 when nothing matches <log> is a file name in <project>/logs/ , or a path when it contains / . Patterns are grep basic regular expressions and are case-sensitive. --no-color (or the NO_COLOR environment variable) turns off colours. The script uses only commands that behave the same with GNU and BSD tools, so it works on Linux and macOS.

docs.text: Project layout ¶ Where the scripts expect the project, where they put builds and logs, and what CMake receives from them. Folders ¶ examples/esp32/ the ESP-IDF project ("project directory") ├── CMakeLists.txt ├── app_config.yml read by every script ├── main/ the app sources named in app_config.yml ├── scripts/ this repository (submodule) ├── builds/ created by build_app.sh, one folder per build ├── logs/ created by flash_app.sh --log └── secrets.local.yml optional, ESP-NOW pairing secret (keep it out of git) How the project is found ¶ Way Project directory Nothing set The folder above the script ( scripts/.. ) --project-path <path> ( build_app.sh , flash_app.sh , manage_idf.sh ) That path, relative to the current directory or absolute PROJECT_PATH=<path> in the environment Same as the flag; the flag sets this variable --project-path / -p ( generate_matrix.py , get_app_info.py ) That path With a path set, config_loader.sh stops with an error when <path>/app_config.yml does not exist. manage_logs.sh , idf_flash_monitor.sh and setup_common.sh always use scripts/.. . Build folders ¶ Every build has its own folder, so switching app, build type or ESP-IDF version never reuses another build's cache: <project>/builds/<build_config.build_directory_pattern> The placeholders {app_type} , {build_type} , {target} and {idf_version} are replaced; the ESP-IDF version has / and . turned into _ ( release/v5.5 becomes release_v5_5 ). Without yq , or when the key is missing, the pattern build-app-{app_type}-type-{build_type}-target-{target}-idf-{idf_version} is used. What CMake receives ¶ build_app.sh runs idf.py -B <build folder> reconfigure and then build with: Variable Value APP_TYPE The app name from app_config.yml BUILD_TYPE , CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE The build type, for example Debug APP_SOURCE_FILE The app's source_file (or the first of source_files ), from get_app_info.py IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE 1 unless --no-cache or USE_CCACHE=0 ESPNOW_PAIRING_SECRET_HEX Only when a pairing secret is configured ( below ) ESP-IDF configures components once without these variables (the requirements phase), so a component that reads them needs a default. setup_basic.sh writes a project that does this: main/CMakeLists.txt (from setup_basic.sh) if ( NOT DEFINED APP_SOURCE_FILE ) if ( CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR STREQUAL CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR ) set ( APP_SOURCE_FILE "${DEFAULT_SOURCE_FILE}" ) # requirements phase else () message ( FATAL_ERROR "APP_SOURCE_FILE not defined. Please use build_app.sh to build this project." ) endif () endif () idf_component_register ( SRCS "${APP_SOURCE_FILE}" REQUIRES driver esp_timer freertos log ) target_compile_definitions ( ${ COMPONENT_LIB } PRIVATE "APP_TYPE_${APP_TYPE}=1" ) ESP-NOW pairing secret ¶ Projects that pair boards over ESP-NOW take a 32-hex-character secret. build_app.sh looks, in order, at --secret <hex> , the ESPNOW_PAIRING_SECRET environment variable and espnow_pairing_secret: in <project>/secrets.local.yml , and passes the first one it finds as ESPNOW_PAIRING_SECRET_HEX . A value that is not 32 hex characters stops the build. With none, a Release build prints a warning and continues. Generate one with openssl rand -hex 16 . Next: app_config.yml .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Add the scripts to an ESP-IDF project, describe one app and build and flash it. You need git, Python 3 with PyYAML, and either an installed ESP-IDF or the network access to let the scripts install one (see Setting up a machine ). yq is optional; without it the scripts parse app_config.yml with grep and sed and a few features fall back to defaults ( config_loader.sh ). Add the scripts next to the project, as a submodule: cd examples/esp32 # the folder with the project's CMakeLists.txt git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-espidf-project-tools.git scripts The scripts take the folder above them as the project. To keep them elsewhere, pass --project-path ; see Project layout . docs.text: Setting up a machine ¶ Install the toolchain on a development machine, or start a new project with the scripts already in place. setup_repo.sh: a development machine ¶ Run once per machine, from a project that contains the scripts, as a normal user with sudo : ./scripts/setup_repo.sh After a confirmation prompt it installs, in order: System packages for Ubuntu, Fedora, CentOS or macOS (build tools, libraries). The Clang 20 tools (compiler, clang-format , clang-tidy ). yq . Every ESP-IDF version in the project's metadata.idf_versions ( release/v5.5 when there is no app_config.yml ) into ~/esp/esp-idf-<version> . The Python packages. Aliases in ~/.bashrc : get_idf , build_app , flash_app , list_apps . It then checks the installation. Then: cd my-esp-idf-project ./scripts/build_app.sh main_app Release setup_common.sh ¶ The functions both scripts use (OS detection, package installation, ESP-IDF install and export, environment setup). build_app.sh sources it to install a missing ESP-IDF version. It is not run directly. Python packages ¶ requirements.txt lists what the Python scripts and the CI need: pyyaml , esptool , pyserial , esp-idf-kconfig , esp-idf-size . pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ What checks this repository, and how to run the tests. Tests ¶ tests/test_scripts.sh checks the scripts' behaviour without ESP-IDF, network or a board: the ESP-IDF folder names manage_idf.sh uses, every manage_logs.sh command, the build_config defaults in config_loader.sh , every get_app_info.py command, and that no script relies on GNU-only find -printf or stat -c . Each test runs in its own temporary folder (with HOME pointed there for manage_idf.sh ). It needs only bash 3.2 or later; the get_app_info.py tests also need python3 with PyYAML and are skipped without it. ./tests/test_scripts.sh # all tests; exit status is the number of failures ./tests/test_scripts.sh logs # only tests whose name contains "logs" tests/test_tab_completion.sh checks the tab completion: installation into ~/.bashrc , app and build-type discovery from app_config.yml , port discovery and simulated completions. tests/demo_tab_completion.sh shows the completions interactively. Both expect the scripts inside a project ( examples/esp32/scripts ). cd examples/esp32/scripts/tests ./test_tab_completion.sh The build and flash scripts are exercised by every repository that builds its ESP32 examples in CI through hf-espidf-ci-tools . CI workflows ¶ Workflow Checks ci-docs-publish.yml Strict site build, generated tables and figure drift, link check, Lighthouse; publishes the site from main ; a single CI gate check yamllint.yml YAML style ( .yamllint , strict) script-tests.yml tests/test_scripts.sh on Ubuntu (GNU tools) and macOS (BSD tools, bash 3.2); on pull requests only when a script, test or the workflow changes The first two call the versioned workflows of hf-general-ci-tools at @v1 . After editing an argument of generate_matrix.py or get_app_info.py , refresh the tables on this site: hardfoc-docs gen
